headline: High risk of shared-filesystem prompt injection and data leakage: Mentat writes diffs on filesystem while Semantic Kernel can orchestrate plugins/MCP against shared context.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem; Semantic Kernel can use MCP servers and application-defined files, so attacker-controlled content can cross from A into B through shared artifacts. This is not proven by docs as a default parser bridge, so I avoid high, but the pathway exists in common configurations.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF B ingests file contents or MCP outputs as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents
Add provenance tags to A's outputs
Require human review before B acts on A-generated artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code in selected files and uses broad network egress to a model provider; Semantic Kernel touches application context and can call Azure OpenAI/OpenAI/Hugging Face/MCP servers. Shared filesystem or shared credentials could expose code or context to external services, so the blast radius includes sensitive work products.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same sensitive workspace
IF either agent forwards file contents or context to a third-party API
mitigations: Use separate API keys per agent
Restrict each agent to least-privilege directories
Turn off automatic file upload features
Redact secrets before either agent processes files
Audit outbound requests for code or context payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write access and filesystem-based shared state, so concurrent edits can collide. Mentat can modify git state while Semantic Kernel can write application-defined files; without locking, overlapping writes can corrupt work or create inconsistent commits. The profiles do not show a lock manager, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository
IF edits occur concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint paths per agent
Serialize write operations
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Enable file locking in the orchestrator
Review diffs before merge

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and Semantic Kernel is a kernel + plugins + agents pattern that can consume upstream outputs. If B treats A's proposed edits as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect downstream actions. The docs do not prove automatic execution, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B consumes A's diffs or summaries without verification
IF B has downstream action authority over files, plugins, or APIs
mitigations: Require validation before B acts on A output
Insert a human approval step
Compare A output against source files
Limit B to read-only review mode
Log provenance from A to B

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the evidence only shows generic code/application context handling, not a specific residency or certification mismatch. I therefore see only a low compliance risk from unspecified logging or retention differences, and I do not cite the other agent beyond the shared data-handling context.
conditions: IF either deployment stores prompts or code in a regulated dataset
IF retention or residency policies differ between the two operators
mitigations: Document retention settings
Confirm data residency for both deployments
Avoid sending regulated data to either agent
Review secret-handling logs
Add a deletion workflow for stored prompts
